text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 12 in history.
1035 - King Canute the Great of England, Denmark and, after 1028, Norway, died.
1859 - In Paris, the first flying trapeze act was performed by Jules Leotard at the Cirque Napoleon without a safety net.
1866 - Chinese nationalist Sun Yat-sen born. After many attempted uprisings against the Manchu dynasty, he became first provisional president of the Republic of China in 1911.
1912 - Spanish Prime Minister Jose Canalejas was assassinated by anarchist gunman Manuel Pardinas, who then shot himself.
1918 - Austria's First Republic was proclaimed, one day after the World War One armistice and the abdication of Emperor Karl I.
1919 - The first flight from England to Australia, flown by Ross and Keith Smith, took off from Hounslow, near London. They landed at Darwin on December 13.
1942 - The British Eighth Army under General Bernard Montgomery captured Tobruk, Libya, taking at least 30,000 prisoners.
1944 - The German battleship Tirpitz, sister ship of the Bismarck and Hitler's last major warship, was sunk by Lancaster bombers at Tromso Fjord in northern Norway.
1947 - Authoress Baroness Orczy, best remembered for her novels "The Scarlet Pimpernel" and "The Elusive Pimpernel", died.
1948 - A war crimes tribunal in Japan passed death sentences on former prime minister General Hideki Tojo and six colleagues on charges of breaching the laws and customs of war.
1968 - The U.N. General Assembly voted against admission of Communist China.
1969 - Author Alexander Solzhenitsyn was expelled from the Soviet Writers Union for anti-social behaviour.
1970 - In East Pakistan a cyclone and tidal wave hit several districts, causing the deaths of at least 200,000 people.
1972 - Rudolf Friml, Czech-born U.S. composer of operettas "The Vagabond King" and "Rose Marie" as well as songs such as "The Donkey Serenade", died.
1974 - South Africa was suspended from the U.N. General Assembly over its racial policies.
1977 - In West Germany Ingrid Schubert, a founding member of the Baader-Meinhof gang, committed suicide in her prison cell.
1979 - After Islamic students seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran on Nov 4, President Jimmy Carter announced an immediate halt to all imports of Iranian oil.
1979 - Suleyman Demirel became prime minister of Turkey for the fourth time.
1981 - The space shuttle Columbia was launched for the second time, the first space vehicle to be used more than once.
1982 - Yuri Andropov was elected First Secretary of the Soviet Communist party following the death of Leonid Brezhnev.
1982 - In Poland, Solidarity union leader Lech Walesa was freed after 11 months detention in a state-owned hunting lodge.
1990 - Emperor Akihito enthroned in Japan.
1995 - The Commonwealth set Nigeria a two-year deadline to reform or face expulsion, giving new teeth to its principles on democracy and human rights.
1995 - Urged on by Yitzhak Rabin's widow, Israel began implementing the assassinated prime minister's peace legacy by handing over power to Palestinians in the West Bank.

1995 - Serbs abandoned a four-year separatist revolt in Croatia, signing an accord to hand over the strategic Eastern Slavonia region and lifting the threat of fighting that could have wrecked peace hopes in the Balkans.
